fluff.overview:
The Jackal is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced in 3052, designed by the Solaris VII-based Vining Engineering and Salvage Team and manufactured in quantity by Earthwerks BattleMechs at their Keystone facility in the Free Worlds League. Drawing on first-hand research of Clan engagements during the initial invasion, VEST set out to create an Inner Sphere light 'Mech capable of matching Clan designs of comparable tonnage on the battlefield.

The Jackal saw widespread service with Capellan and Free Worlds League forces as well as numerous mercenary commands throughout the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras. One of many casualties of the Word of Blake Jihad, all Jackal production ceased in 3079, leaving surviving chassis scattered among garrison and mercenary units across the Inner Sphere.
fluff.capabilities:
The Jackal was built on a weight-saving Hollis Mark VI-Alpha endo steel chassis and powered by a GM 210 XL engine, enabling a top speed of nearly 120 kilometers per hour. This lightweight construction freed tonnage for armament and protection impressive for a thirty-ton design. Six tons of York Industries CTC-0 armor provide solid coverage for the weight class, though the lack of CASE remains a persistent vulnerability should ammunition storage be breached.

The Jackal's primary weapon is an Aberdovey Mark XXX extended-range particle cannon, giving the light 'Mech reach comparable to most Clan weaponry at just under 700 meters. A Holly Streak SRM-2 launcher provides efficient close-range backup, firing only when a solid target lock is achieved, while a head-mounted Burrow anti-missile system offers limited defense against incoming missiles. This combination of speed, firepower, and point defense enables the Jackal to operate as a highly mobile long-range sniper, engaging targets at distance while minimizing exposure to return fire.

The reliance on single heat sinks remains the design's most notable shortcoming, limiting sustained fire from the energy-hungry particle cannon and forcing pilots to carefully manage their rate of engagement.
fluff.history:
The Jackal's story begins on Solaris VII, where VEST leveraged first-hand observations of Clan technology gathered during the initial invasion to design a light 'Mech capable of competing with Clan designs pound for pound. The prototype's successful demonstration in the Solaris arenas in 3052 caught the attention of Earthwerks Incorporated, who struck a deal with VEST for production rights at their Keystone plant in the Free Worlds League. Under the agreement, VEST retained limited production capacity on Solaris VII to supply arena stables and select buyers, while Earthwerks handled volume manufacturing for military customers.

The Jackal quickly found favor with the Capellan Confederation and Free Worlds League armed forces, as well as dozens of mercenary commands throughout the Inner Sphere. The design's combination of speed and long-range firepower made it particularly effective in the skirmishing and raiding operations that characterized the post-invasion era. During Operation Bulldog and the subsequent invasion of Huntress in 3060, the Jackal proved capable in direct engagements against Clan Smoke Jaguar forces, with pilots reporting success even against the then-novel ProtoMechs that accompanied Jaguar defensive formations.

The FedCom Civil War saw continued production at both facilities, but the Jihad proved devastating for the entire Jackal program. VEST's Solaris VII operations were heavily damaged during the fighting that engulfed the Game World, and while limited production resumed around 3074, the destruction of the planet's HPG severed communications between VEST and Earthwerks. By the late Jihad, Earthwerks was emphasizing its own engineering contributions to the Jackal program with no mention of VEST, and the partnership effectively dissolved.

The subsequent cessation of all Jackal production in 3079 left the remaining chassis scattered among mercenary and garrison units, maintained by field technicians but no longer supported by any manufacturer. Earthwerks' brief attempt to develop upgraded refit kits for the design came too late to save the program, and the Jackal joined the growing list of Jihad-era production casualties.
fluff.deployment: An experimental field refit kit developed by Earthwerks near their Keystone facility, this variant was first sighted in 3077 during the final years of the Jihad. Designed as an upgrade package for existing JA-KL-1532 chassis, the refit addressed several long-standing complaints about the original design. The conversion replaces the Streak SRM-2 launcher and its ammunition with a PPC capacitor, boosting the Aberdovey particle cannon's output by fifty percent, while an Angel ECM suite provides electronic warfare protection against Word of Blake C-cubed systems and other electronic threats. The switch to double heat sinks and ferro-fibrous armor panels further modernizes the platform. Production was extremely limited, as the cooperation between Earthwerks and VEST had broken down and all Jackal production ceased by 3079, effectively ending the 1579 program before it could achieve wide distribution. Earthwerks also offered a cut-price variant kit designated the JA-KL-1578, which traded the rare Angel ECM for a more common Guardian suite and added an ER small laser.
